_note: Knobs for the collector's memory (experiments/browser_scout/collector_memory.py). Every one of these exists because the loop had none of it and spent 3 days re-reading 4 pages on 1 axis.
_seen_ttl_days: A URL already rejected for the same axis + need class is not re-read for this many days. After it, the record is stale and the page is read again regardless of its hash — the world moves.
_hash_probe: Inside the TTL, one cheap plain-HTTP GET decides whether the page CHANGED. If it did, the skip is lifted and the page is read properly. One GET is far less than a browser page-load plus two local-model votes, which is what the skip saves.
_max_query_attempts: A query that produced 0 components may not be reused. After this many attempts to produce a fresh one, the run ends with a named refusal instead of repeating.
_dry_runs_before_rotation: Consecutive runs producing 0 components after which an axis yields its slot to another hungry axis. Round-robin, and if every axis is over the limit the one waiting longest goes anyway — starvation is not a fix for repetition.
